newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-UK M4 money supply seen stable in August.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-UK M4 money supply seen stable in August.

text.p: UK broad money supply growth should hold steady in August, suggesting July's sharp fall was a one-off, analysts said on Tuesday.

A Reuter poll of economists forecast M4 money supply growth of 9.0 percent year-on-year, right at the top of the government's three-to-nine percent monitoring range, and reflecting a 0.7 percent monthly rise.
"July's sharp decline in M4 growth should not be taken as indicating the start of a downward trend," said Ciaran Barr, UK economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

In July, M4 growth dropped to 9.0 percent year-on-year from 9.9 the month before. A public sector debt repayment of 1.66 billion stg in July combined with heavy gilt sales to reduce the money supply, Barr said.
August's public sector borrowing requirement, released on Tuesday, totalled 4.53 billion stg, suggesting that effect will not be repeated.
"Accordingly, we expect M4 growth to remain at or around the upper end of the government's monitoring range in coming months," Barr said.
August figures will be released on Thursday at 0830 GMT.
Michael Saunders, UK economist at Salomon Brothers, said July's year-on-year M4 figure was also depressed by a sharp rise in M4 the previous July. That too will not be repeated, he said.

Analysts said M4 lending will remain robust in August as British consumers remain eager to spend and willing to borrow to do so. The consensus forecast is for lending to increase by 5.4 billion stg in August.
"M4 lending remains robust and should continue to do so, aided by increasing personal sector mortgage borrowing," Barr said.

Saunders said building society net new commitments data, released alongside the M4 numbers, will show mortgage lending stayed at high levels in August. In July, mortgage lending rose to the highest level in nearly six years.

Saunders forecast net new approvals worth 3.8 billion stg in August, flat to July's figure. "Such a reading would put commitments well up from a year ago, and imply that mortgage loans and turnover will continue to rise in the coming months."
"Further, recent data from the banking industry suggests that mortgage lending is picking up along with the recovery in the housing market," Royal Bank of Scotland economist Marian Bell said.

She forecast M4 money supply growth of 9.2 percent year-on-year in August, noting that the unwinding of the effects of the Glaxo-Wellcome merger and Lloyds Bank's takeover of the Cheltenham & Gloucester building society suppressed M4 growth in August last year.
